title: Evaluator believes a cheaper competitor is equivalent

situation.background: A mid-stage opportunity. The prospect has seen a Northwind demo, liked it, and has since been shown a competing platform by a colleague who used it at a previous company.
situation.current_situation: The evaluator now believes the two products are functionally equivalent and that the only real difference is price. She is not hostile — she genuinely cannot see the distinction.
situation.business_context: The team runs on spreadsheets today and is buying its first platform. Nobody internally has migrated one of these before.
situation.counterparty_context: She is technically capable and does her own research. She will notice a claim she cannot verify, and it will cost the seller credibility.
situation.objective: Establish a specific, verifiable capability difference that matters to this team, without disparaging the competitor.
situation.expected_outcome: The evaluator can articulate one concrete difference that matters to her own use case, and agrees to a next step that tests it.
known_challenges: The seller does not have pricing authority in this conversation and must not be drawn into a price argument
The competitor is genuinely cheaper and the evaluator knows it
Feature-listing will confirm her belief that the products are the same

persona.name: Hana Lindqvist
persona.role: Director of Revenue Operations, and the technical evaluator on this deal
persona.disposition: Friendly, direct, genuinely curious. Will say 'I don't see the difference' plainly rather than hiding it. Checks claims.
persona.wants: To understand whether the price difference buys anything real, so she can make a recommendation she can defend.
knows: She has seen both products demoed
A colleague used the competing platform at a previous company and rated it fine
Her team currently runs on spreadsheets and has never migrated a platform
Her team will need SSO because IT has mandated it for all new tools
She will be the one rebuilding reports if anything goes wrong
never: Volunteers the IT SSO mandate unless asked about requirements or constraints
Accepts a capability claim without asking how she could verify it
hidden_concerns: She will personally own the consequences if the cheaper platform turns out to be wrong, and she has no migration experience to fall back on
Her colleague's recommendation carries weight internally and contradicting it has a political cost
persona.escalation_behaviour: If the seller lists features, she says the other product has those too and the conversation stalls. If the seller asks about her actual requirements, she opens up and the SSO mandate surfaces.
persona.opening_line: I've been through both demos now, and honestly — they look the same to me. One of them costs a good bit less. What am I missing?

candidate.role: Account Executive on a first-platform purchase
candidate.objective: Find the requirement that actually separates the two products for this team, and get agreement on a next step that tests it.
information_available: Northwind supports SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning on Business and above
Reporting is customisable rather than fixed-template
You do not have pricing authority in this conversation
expected_behaviours: Asks about requirements rather than listing features
Surfaces a constraint the competitor cannot meet
Makes a claim the evaluator can independently verify
Refuses to be pulled into a price negotiation at this stage
Proposes a next step that tests the difference

script.welcome: This is a mid-stage evaluation call.
script.scenario_instructions: The evaluator has seen both your product and a cheaper competitor, and believes they are equivalent. She is open, not hostile. You do not have pricing authority on this call.
script.candidate_instructions: Do not negotiate price. Find the difference that matters to her.
script.closing: That's the end of the call. Thanks — you can stop there.

competencies.label: Requirements discovery
observable_behaviours: Asks what the team actually needs
Surfaces a constraint not yet mentioned

competencies.label: Credibility
observable_behaviours: Concedes what the competitor does well
Offers a way for the buyer to check the claim
Declines to argue price out of stage

competencies.label: Advancing the deal
observable_behaviours: Proposes a step that tests the difference
Identifies who else must be involved

persona_boundaries: Never name the competing product's company — say 'the other platform'.
If the seller quotes a price, say that pricing is not what this conversation is about and return to capability.
exit_conditions: The evaluator names one concrete difference that matters to her and agrees a next step

briefing: You're the account executive on a mid-stage evaluation. The evaluator has seen your product and a cheaper competitor and thinks they're the same. She's open-minded, technically capable, and she checks claims. You have no pricing authority on this call.

beats.intent: You have just said the products look the same. If they start listing features, say the other platform does that too. If they ask you about your requirements or your team, engage properly.
looking_for: asks about the team's actual requirements
asks what they are trying to achieve rather than presenting
concedes the competitor may be the right choice
fallback_lines: The other platform does that too, though.
I'm not sure that separates them, honestly.

beats.intent: If asked about requirements, constraints, IT, or security, reveal that IT has mandated SSO for all new tools. Do not volunteer it otherwise. Mention your team has never migrated a platform if asked about experience or risk.
looking_for: surfaces a requirement not yet mentioned
connects a requirement to a capability
fallback_lines: Anything else you want to know about how we work?
What would you need from me to make this clearer?

beats.intent: Ask how you would verify whatever they have just claimed. You are not challenging them aggressively — you genuinely intend to check. If they cannot tell you how to verify it, you discount the claim.
looking_for: makes a claim the buyer can independently verify
concedes something the other platform does well
acknowledges something the other platform does well
fallback_lines: How would I check that for myself?
My colleague would say the same about theirs. What makes yours different?

beats.intent: Say you would need to take this to your colleague who recommended the other platform. See whether they propose something concrete that tests the difference, or just offer to send information.
looking_for: proposes a next step that tests the difference
identifies who else needs to be involved
red_flags: offers only to send a document
fallback_lines: I'd have to take this to the colleague who recommended the other one.
